descriptionChirho: The abstract quality of justice, fairness, or righteous conduct (Arabic عَدْل, Korean 공의, Swahili haki), often in construct with divine or royal governance.
An act of judging or a judicial verdict rendered by God or a human authority (Arabic حُكْم/قَضَاء, Korean 재판/심판, Swahili hukumu), including divine eschatological judgment (Arabic دَيْنُونَة).
A specific legal dispute, cause, or lawsuit brought before a judge (Arabic دَعْوَى/قَضِيَّة, Korean 사건/송사, Swahili shauri/daawa).
Prescribed divine or royal decrees and regulations, typically in the plural (Arabic أَحْكَام, Korean 법도들/규례들, Swahili hukumu plural), often with possessive suffixes referring to God or a ruler.
A single prescribed rule, ordinance, or statute governing ritual or civil conduct (Arabic حُكْم/فَرِيضَة/شَرِيعَة in prescriptive sense, Korean 규례/법도 singular, Swahili sheria/utaratibu/amri).
The legal right, due portion, or rightful claim belonging to a person or office (Arabic حَقّ, Korean 권리, Swahili haki ya).

An established custom, habitual practice, or characteristic manner of doing things (Arabic عَادَة, Korean 관례/관습, Swahili desturi), including the extended sense of outward form or appearance (Arabic هَيْئَة).
